summary.title: A plain english introduction to CAP Theorem
summary.one_liner: The CAP theorem says a distributed system cannot guarantee consistency, availability, and partition tolerance all at once, and you can only pick two, illustrated with a phone-based remembering business run by a husband and wife.
takeaways: CAP states that a distributed system can guarantee only two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.
Consistency means every client gets the latest updated data regardless of which node answers.
Availability means the system keeps answering requests while some nodes are down; partition tolerance means it keeps working when nodes cannot communicate.
Eventual consistency, where a background process syncs nodes, trades short-term consistency for availability and partition tolerance.
summary.summary: The article uses a story about a "Remembrance Inc" phone service run by a husband and wife to explain the CAP theorem in plain language. The author walks through a design that fails on consistency, then one that adds availability, and then shows that handling partitions (lost communication between the two people) forces a choice between consistency and availability. It closes by describing a background-sync approach, which it links to eventual consistency in NoSQL systems.
